text:
Maya (CEO): Thanks everyone for joining the all-hands. Opening this thread for quick follow-ups on mission, positioning, and next steps. Keep Qs short, we'll reply through the day.

Priya (Head of Product): Quick clarification: when we say 'unified runtime', is that an external promise or an internal engineering abstraction customers will see?

Jon (CTO): It's both. Externally it's a promise (same API, consistent SLOs), internally it maps to routing, cache, and kernel selection layers. Customers only need to configure a policy.

Aisha (PMM): Need a short claim for marketing: one sentence that captures mission without being too engineering-y.

Maya (CEO): Draft for PMM: "Make inference predictable and cost-effective everywhere — hosted, reserved, or private." Aisha feel free to iterate.

Kevin (Eng): On the roadmap: can we confirm priority order for next two quarters: 1) latency kernel improvements, 2) rollout and canaries, 3) cost dashboard enhancements?

Priya (Head of Product): That's the plan, but we may reorder small items based on customer escalations. Kernel work targets high-throughput tiers first.

Liam (Support): From field: prospects ask about 'model zoo' vs our offering. What's the quick response?

Maya (CEO): Acknowledge model choice is important. Our distinction: we don't just host models — we run them reliably at scale with controls over latency/cost and enterprise integrations (KMS, audit logs, SLAs).

Kevin (Eng): Can we add a short code demo for sales that shows fallback behavior? Small snippet to paste in slides.

Jon (CTO): Use this YAML example: 
```nroute_policy:
  prefer: low_latency
  fallback: quantized_small
  cache_prefix: true
```
Explains behavior without deep infra talk.

Aisha (PMM): Any guidance on competitor messaging where they promise 'latest weights daily'?

Maya (CEO): Say: freshness is great, but rolling models into production without performance guarantees leads to outages and cost surprises. We partner to onboard new weights with measurable SLO gates.

Priya (Head of Product): Action item: I'll capture the "winning metrics" doc we discussed and share a Confluence link by EOD.

DeployBot: Release notes for canary rollout tooling uploaded: https://internal.redwood/release/2026-03-canary-tooling

Kevin (Eng): Regarding triggers for sales outreach: current rule of thumb was >$5k/mo usage or repeated p95 breaches. Can we formalize those?

Maya (CEO): Yes — formalize and add to the Customer Playbook. @Priya please add a short checklist.

Liam (Support): For objections on cost vs doing self-hosting: is there a quick ROI line?

Maya (CEO): Use a comparison: "Redwood reduces infra ops and amortized GPU spend through batching, caching, and optimized kernels — typically 30-60% lower TCO vs unmanaged fleets for comparable throughput." (Numbers are illustrative; send to finance for precise benchmarks.)

Aisha (PMM): Marketing ask: can we get a small set of verified performance numbers we can publish? Need a safe set (not too broad).

Jon (CTO): We'll provide median latency and cost per 1k tokens for two common model classes (open-encoder, decoder-only) next week.

Priya (Head of Product): Last: who owns customer-facing docs updates about routing policies?

Kevin (Eng): Eng-docs will draft, Priya will review, Aisha will sign off for tone.

Maya (CEO): Great. I'll compile these action items and ping stakeholders. If anyone has more follow-ups, drop them here or DM. Thanks! :heart:
